title: C482/1172/2024 of MANISH BHANDARI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
SL.
No Date
Office Notes, reports,
orders or proceedings
or directions and
Registrar's order with
Signatures
COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
(Compounding Appl. No.01 of 2024)
In
C 482 No.1172 of 2024
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Lalit Sharma, learned counsel for the
applicant.
2. Mr. Bhaskar Chandra Joshi, learned AGA
for the State.
3. Mr. P.C. Petshali, learned counsel for
respondent no.2.
4. Present C482 application has been
preferred along with compounding application,
which is supported with the affidavits of
applicant and respondent no.2.
5. Applicant and respondent no.2 are present,
in person, before this Court. They are duly
identified by their respective counsel.
6. This is a case in which present applicant is
facing trial in Criminal Case No.196 of 2022 for
the offences punishable under Section 376, 313
& 506 IPC arising out of FIR/Crime No.155 of
2021 dated 02.05.2021, P.S. Nehru Colony,
District Dehradun, pending in the court of Chief
Judicial Magistrate, Dehradun.
7. The allegation, as alleged in the FIR,
appears to be on the false pretext of marriage.
It appears from the FIR itself that both the
applicant and respondent no.2 were friends
since long back.
8. This Court interacted with respondent
no.2/complainant and the applicant. On
interaction, respondent no.2 submits that infact,
applicant is her old friend and he has married
with another lady and now she wants to marry
somewhere else, therefore, she does not want
to proceed with this case. She, on interaction,
further submits that continuation of this
proceeding will effect her future as well as the
present applicant.
9. Learned State Counsel submits that the
respondent no.2-prosecutrix herself does not
want to pursue this case since she has settled

the dispute with the applicant and further as per
allegation, is her old friend, and both of them
have entered into compromise and settled their
dispute amicably, therefore, compounding
application can be allowed. He further submits
that now since the respondent no.2-complainant
herself does not want to pursue the
proceedings, therefore, there is no useful
purpose to continue with the proceedings, as
there are very remote chances of conviction of
applicant. However, he submits that while
compounding the offence some cost would be
imposed.
10. I found force in the submission advanced
by the State Counsel. After hearing learned
counsel for the parties and taking into
consideration the compromise entered between
the parties, since respondent no.2/complainant
herself does not want to pursue with this case
and she want to settle her life to marry with
someone else and she is well educated and
furthermore, applicant is now married, this
Court is of the view that compounding
application deserves to be allowed with the cost
of Rs.2,00,000/- lakhs. Accordingly,
compounding application is allowed with the cost
of Rs.2,00,000/- lakhs.
11. Applicant, who is present in the Court, is
agree to pay the cost of Rs.2,00,000/-to the
respondent no.2 within one month.
12. Subject to the cost, as above, the entire
proceedings of Criminal Case No.196 of 2022
(State Vs. Manish Bhandari), arising out of FIR
No.155 of 2021, punishable for the offences
under Section 376, 313 and 506 of IPC pending
in the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Dehradun are quashed.
13. Accordingly, C482 application also stands
disposed of.
